messages.subject: Pirkan Fluid Systems and three buyers in the Nordics
messages.body:
Jukka,

I am writing because of your dosing systems. Pirkan Fluid Systems has something most Nordic pump companies never built: a thirty-year installed base in pulp and paper mills and municipal waterworks, and a PFS Care service business that repeats every year.

We are working with three buyers looking for this profile in the Nordics. A lower mid-market fund building an industrial services platform, a listed engineering group adding aftermarket businesses, and a Finnish family office that holds for decades. None of them has heard your name from us.

I run Mergero, an M&A advisory firm in Helsinki. We have closed over 500 million euros of transactions, all off-market, no auctions.

Would a 30-minute call next week be worth your time? Even if the answer is not now, you will know where the market stands.

Timo Tontti
Managing Partner, Mergero

transcript.text: Good evening, Herr Brandl. I work with Timo Tontti at Mergero. This conversation is confidential and only Timo sees it. I have four short questions to prepare your call on Wednesday. First: roughly how does Traxio's revenue split between recurring managed services, project work, and hardware or licence resale?
Roughly 68 percent managed services including the SOC, about 24 percent projects and integration, the rest hardware and licences, maybe 8 percent. The managed share has grown every year since 2019.
Thank you. How concentrated is the client base? A rough share for your largest client and for the top ten together is enough.
The largest is the machine-tool group, around 13 percent. Top ten together perhaps 40 percent, I would say 41. Nobody else is above 6 percent.
Understood. On profitability: the 2.4 million EBITDA in the accounts, are there items you would consider one-off or owner-related that a buyer should add back?

Yes. My salary is above market by maybe 250 thousand. Regensburg cost us about 200 thousand in 2025 before it broke even, and the SOC set-up had one-off costs. Normalised I would say 2.9 to 3.0 million.

That is helpful. Last question, in two parts. What would an ideal outcome look like for you personally over the next two years, and is there anything that would make you walk away from a deal regardless of price?

Sign within 12 to 18 months, stay up to 24 months for the handover. Stefan wants to continue and would put his own money in if there is a structure for it. I want time for the university board and I want to stop signing personal guarantees for growth. Walk away: anyone who wants to close Regensburg or move the service desk offshore, and no earn-out above 20 percent. I tell the staff myself before anything is announced. One more thing: the Nürnberg office building is mine privately and leased to the company, we should talk about that.
